$Comment: Scope-2 wave-3 leg W3-F (design section 2.7, GATE OUTCOMES m1 fix, decision 40): the flagship multi-station fish exemplar, attached to Server/RpgStations/Stations/CuttingBoard.json via {"Ref":"prepfish"}. Custody.Input is authored explicitly (ResourceTypeId 'Fish', the native family every caught-fish item shares via Template_Fish_Item.json) because this action has no Recipe.Conversions for the usual zero-extra-authoring fallback to derive from - it is a Steps program. M1 FIX (critique-adopted, gate Q3/Q23): the old design draft split fish-scaling into a single step that BOTH consumed the raw fish AND repeated 3x - a Consume inside a Repeat re-executes the consume every iteration, over-draining custody. Fixed here by splitting 'load' (a one-shot Consume, Repeat absent) from 'scale' (a pure Duration BEAT with no Consume phase, Repeat:{Times:3}) - the authoring guide's own footgun callout. Tool gate = the DAGGERS weapon family, RE-AUTHORED onto Tags.Family (seam wave, decision 53's MQ7 redirection, superseding gate decision 40's Ids enumeration): a scout confirmed vanilla weapons carry native Tags {Type:['Weapon'],Family:['Dagger']} on their shared Template_Weapon_Daggers.json parent, inherited to every material tier at decode time (appendInherited) - Tags.Family:['Dagger'] is the ANY-of match every Daggers tier satisfies with ZERO per-tier enumeration (a future dagger tier just works, matching the Anvil's own preference for the native-category composition shape over a hand-maintained id list; runtime read is Item.getData().getRawTags()). Anchors.fire targets the 'cookingfire' station (Server/RpgStations/Stations/CookingFire.json) within a 12-block radius (the design-2.2 default MaxRadius). Work.Repeat:true + the engine's new StopReason.INPUTS_EXHAUSTED (design 2.4) is 'repeats while fish remain' with zero mode flags - the session ends gracefully once no more Fish custody remains at the next 'load' step's Consume. Sound/particle/emote ids are all REAL, already-shipped-elsewhere ids (verified against the shared source / this repo's own usage), never invented placeholders: Smoke_Black (Deco_Campfire_Off.json's own particle), SFX_Player_Drop_Item (the vanilla generic item-place sound), RPG_Emote_Knife (this jar's own Server/Emote/RPG_Emote_Knife.json). AV WAVE (maintainer's post-smoke cue pass) - every added id is likewise real and one-shot (never a Looping SoundEvent: nothing in the protocol can stop a playing sound, so a looping id fired through a step Presentation would never end): 'scale' swapped its whoosh for SFX_Daggers_T1_Slash_Impact (the dagger's own blade-LANDS impact - the knife swing is already carried visually by the RPG_Emote_Knife clip, so the audio beat should be the chop landing) plus Block_Hit_Wood chips (the vanilla wood-hit chip+dust system - a knife biting into the wooden board); both re-fire on EACH of the 3 scale beats because StationStepHandlers#emitEntryCues runs inside the per-ITERATION loop, so a Repeat:{Times:3} step cues three times with zero engine change. 'cook' authors Working:true (a pure Duration beat is not a Consume+Produce convert, so it must opt in explicitly) which is what puts the FIRE into its Lit state for exactly this beat, plus SFX_Flame_Ignite as the sizzle one-shot at beat entry (Sounds/Items/Torch/Torch_On.ogg - the flare of food meeting hot coals). 'harvest' gets a deliberately SILENT steam puff (Block_Break_Dust: a bounded 2-particle Smoke_Cartoon burst rendered BlendAdd, so it reads bright/white and dissipates in ~0.5s) - PROVISIONAL, the one visually-approximate id in this pass, because the shared source ships no standalone steam/vapor particlesystem at all (the only vapour in the game is a Vapor_Water SPAWNER nested inside Workbench_Cooking_On, not referenceable as a SystemId). AV-WAVE SMOKE FIX (round 2): Custody.Display was MISSING, so a fish placed on the cutting board rendered nothing at all - the board looked empty while holding custody. Added, following the sawmill's own display conventions (Offset/Rotation are facing-relative to the placed block's yaw, so a Y-ONLY offset stays orientation-safe at any block rotation; the sawmill uses Offset.Y -0.1 / Scale 0.4, the cooking fire Offset.Y 0.4 / Scale 1.0). Offset.Y 0.05 (a fish laid just above the board's top face) and Scale 0.5 (a fish item is small next to a log) are PROVISIONAL - in-game tuning is expected, exactly as the sawmill's and anvil's own values were tuned in-game.
